- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–7 days post-spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; increase forecast downward by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to overcorrect downward; adjust upward by 0.5–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture early downward momentum; if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher weight to recent sentiment if >0.5, lower if <0.4.
